sink: asyncio.create_subprocess_shell(command) in esp_utils.run_command_async() -- runs through a shell
guard: partial: sdkconfig_defaults IS shlex.quote()'d, but idf_path is not
why: export_script = get_export_script(idf_path) = os.path.join(idf_path or $IDF_PATH, 'export.sh') with zero escaping, then f-string-embedded inside a double-quoted bash -c argument that is itself passed to create_subprocess_shell(). idf_path containing a literal '"' breaks out of the double-quoted argument early, exposing the remainder of idf_path as literal shell syntax to the outer shell that runs this whole command line -- e.g. idf_path='x" ; touch /tmp/pwned #' executes the injected touch. The one caller-controlled param that IS escaped (sdkconfig_defaults) shows the developer knew to quote user input elsewhere in the same function, making idf_path's omission a genuine oversight rather than an inherent unescapable design.
contract: Path to ESP-IDF directory. Optional when IDF_PATH environment variable is set.

excerpt: returncode, stdout, stderr = await run_command_async(f"bash -c 'source {export_script} && idf.py create-project --path {project_path} {project_name}'")
why: export_script (from idf_path), project_path, and project_name are all f-string-embedded unescaped inside a single-quoted bash -c argument passed to create_subprocess_shell(). Any of the three containing a literal single quote breaks out of that quoted segment -- e.g. project_name="x'; touch /tmp/pwned; echo '" injects the touch command as literal shell syntax.

excerpt: const result = await this.executeQuery(`CREATE (n:${label} $props) RETURN n`, { props: properties });
sink: session.run(query, params) -- the Neo4j driver's query-execution API
why: properties are correctly bound via Cypher's $props parameter, but label is string-interpolated directly into the Cypher query text (Neo4j labels cannot be parameterised the normal way, so many implementations do this -- but it still means label is fully attacker-controlled Cypher syntax). A label value like 'X) WITH 1 AS x MATCH (a) DETACH DELETE a //' closes the intended clause and appends arbitrary additional Cypher, including destructive operations against the whole graph, executed with whatever privileges this server's Neo4j credentials hold.

guard: partial: isImageSource() requires the string to match an image-filename/extension pattern (or CDN-style path), but performs no path-traversal or directory-containment check
why: The description explicitly invites local file paths ('If it's a local file, do not add any prefix'). isImageSource() only pattern-matches the string against image-extension/CDN-style regexes -- it does not resolve the path or check it against any allowed directory, so a path containing '../' segments that still ends in a recognised image extension (e.g. an existing '*.png' file reachable via traversal) is read with no containment at all. Narrower than an unrestricted read since the target must satisfy the extension pattern, and the compressed output is written server-side rather than returned as raw bytes directly to the caller, which is why this is Tier B rather than A.
